name: Roller XML-RPC
tile_line: Exploited, on CISA's list. No login. Fixed in 6.1.6.
summary: A bug in Apache Roller, a Java blog server, lets anyone who can reach the site send one crafted request to its XML-RPC address and, in the worst case, run their own code, without logging in. Default installs from 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 are affected, even with XML-RPC switched off. Apache rates it Critical (CVSS 9.8) and says it is being actively exploited, and CISA added it to its exploited list (KEV) on 20 Nov 2026; one researcher's public code reaches the bug but says running code on a stock, up-to-date setup needs extra work. 6.1.6 (24 Sep 2026) and later fix it.

affected.label: Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5
affected.text: It's one bug with two CVEs: CVE-2026-129448 covers 4.0.0 through 6.1.4, and CVE-2026-82384 (25 Sep 2026) covers 6.1.5. 6.1.6 and later are fixed. Some news sites name 6.1.5 as the fix; Apache says 6.1.6.

affected.label: XML-RPC extensions still on
affected.text: Every release up to 6.1.5 ships with `enabledForExtensions` set to `true` and `/roller-services/xmlrpc` mapped, so default installs are exposed. Turning XML-RPC off in the admin settings (off by default) does not help. Run this in Roller's webapp folder; `<param-value>true</param-value>` means exposed.

affected.label: Attackers can reach the site
affected.text: One web request to `/roller-services/xmlrpc` is enough. No login and no user action are needed.

do.label: Upgrade to Roller 6.1.7
do.text: 6.1.6 (24 Sep 2026) fixes this bug; 6.1.7 (11 Nov 2026) is the newest and also fixes CVE-2026-123374, a separate deserialization bug in ping responses. Read the 6.1.7 behaviour changes first: for example, Planet is now off by default. Apache doesn't patch older lines.

do.label: Can't upgrade yet?
do.text: In `WEB-INF/web.xml`, set `enabledForExtensions` to `false`, or remove the `/roller-services/xmlrpc` servlet mapping. Then restart Roller. The admin-screen switch alone is not enough.

do.label: Look for signs of attack
do.text: Attacks are POST requests to `/roller-services/xmlrpc`. Apache hasn't published other signs, attacker details or how many sites were hit. If you were exposed, check the server for changes you didn't make.

slack: Apache Roller CVE-2026-129448 (same bug as CVE-2026-82384): anyone who can reach a Roller blog can run code on it without logging in, via crafted XML-RPC requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc. Default installs from 4.0.0 through 6.1.5 are affected, even with XML-RPC turned off in the admin UI. Apache rates it Critical (CVSS 9.8) and says it is being actively exploited (no details given); on CISA KEV since 20 Nov (due 23 Nov). Public proof-of-concept code reaches the bug; the researcher says code execution on a stock, up-to-date setup needs a gadget chain public tools don't provide. Fixed in 6.1.6; upgrade to 6.1.7, the newest. Stopgap: set enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the XML-RPC servlet mapping, then restart.
